resources.string: Keep screen on while Android Auto runs

The most pictures a second the phone sends (1 to 25). Set it to 25 for smooth video: that is the rate the MMI's video stream runs at, so 25 is the limit.

Lower means choppier motion, not less work for the MMI: it fills the gaps by repeating the last picture.

A change applies within about a second, with a short break in the MMI's picture.

How much video data is sent a second. A higher rate keeps text and fast-moving content cleaner. A lower rate sends less over USB. It does not change the picture size.

4 Mbit/s (default) gives sharp text on the car. 2.5 can blur text. 6 gives bigger key frames: if the picture freezes now and then, go back to 4.

A change while streaming applies within about a second.
Keeps the phone\'s screen on (it may dim) while Android Auto runs, even with another app in front. The phone uses more battery with this on.
Android Auto mode is off. Tap Start.

Once, on the phone: open Android Auto\'s settings (button above), tap Version at the bottom about ten times until developer settings are on, then in the menu (three dots) tap Start head unit server. This app connects to it and the MMI shows Android Auto.\n\nTouch the picture above to use Android Auto. Music and navigation sound stay on the phone (Bluetooth to the car).

The picture size Android Auto draws. The app scales it to the MMI's 720x432 (or copies it, 1:1).

800x480: the same shape as the MMI's screen, the whole picture with Android Auto's bar at the bottom.

1280x720 and 1920x1080 (16:9): Android Auto puts its bar in a rail on the left. The MMI shows everything except the rail, filling its screen; the picture here keeps the rail, so tap home, apps and the mic here. Android Auto draws more pixels for the same layout, so text can be sharper. 1920x1080 works the phone harder.

800x480 1:1 (test): Android Auto lays its UI out for the MMI's 720x464 with the rail on the left, and the app copies that part pixel for pixel: no scaling, sharpest text, a full-width map with no bar. If it misbehaves, pick another size.

A new size makes Android Auto reconnect (about 2 seconds).

This app becomes the car's Android Auto display, for Android Auto on this same phone (self mode). The MMI shows Android Auto as H.264, decoded by its video chip, and the picture above is what the MMI shows: touch it to use Android Auto.

Android Auto starts this only through its developer head unit server: Android Auto settings, tap Version until developer settings are on, then menu, Start head unit server. The app tries to connect every 2 seconds and again after every session.

Android Auto draws its screen at the chosen video size, and the app scales it to the MMI's 720x432 picture. It runs at up to 25 frames a second on the MMI. Max fps and H.264 rate below apply.

The mode starts with the app; Stop ends it.
